Hello & Welcome to Snaresbrook Prep!
Our School
Welcome from the Head
A Very Warm Welcome to Snaresbrook Preparatory School
For over eighty years, Snaresbrook Preparatory School has earned a reputation for academic excellence and outstanding pastoral care. These enduring principles were first championed by one of our early Heads, Mrs Mathison, whose guiding question continues to shape all we do: “If this were my child, what would I want for them?”
We are proud to offer a distinctive, independent education for boys and girls aged three-and-a-half to eleven, in an environment where every child is seen, known and heard.
Our purpose is threefold:
To ensure that each child achieves their full academic potential
To nurture character, enabling pupils to do the right thing, in the right way, and for the right reasons
To inspire confidence, independence and a lifelong appetite for learning
Our most recent inspection affirmed the strength of our provision, with inspectors noting that “leaders prioritise pupils’ progress and wellbeing.”
Historically our pupils have moved on to some of the country’s leading senior schools, including Forest, Bancroft’s, Chigwell, and City of London. Wherever they go next, they leave us as curious, confident and kind individuals—well-prepared for all that lies ahead.
In September 2025, Snaresbrook became part of the Forest Group of Schools. Rooted in a shared belief in nurturing, ambitious education, this collaboration with one of London’s foremost 4–18 independent schools enhances our curriculum and broadens opportunities for every pupil.
Crucially, Snaresbrook retains its distinct identity, values and close-knit community. Families will continue to benefit from our individualised approach while enjoying the added advantage of an automatic right of entry to Forest at 11+, subject to academic progress—providing both continuity and choice.
We would be delighted to welcome you for a visit. Please contact our School Office to arrange a personal tour. I look forward to showing you what makes Snaresbrook so special.
Ralph Dalton Headteacher
Curriculum
We take pupils from age three-and-a-half to eleven. Children enter the Nursery and ideally continue through the school to Year 6. All of our classes are small and include both boys and girls.
We provide a rounded primary education covering every aspect of your child’s early development. The curriculum is designed to prepare pupils for public and grammar school entrance and scholarship examinations. Each child is introduced to subjects with great care and sensitivity by working individually, in small groups or with the whole class. We try to find the approach which enables each child to learn and work with enjoyment and enthusiasm and to relate well with fellow pupils.
Admissions
Informal visits allow prospective parents to get a feel for the school and to see the children at work. Parents are invited to organise an informal visit by contacting the office on 020 8989 2394.
If you are interested in applying for a place at our school, for entry at any age, please click the button below where you can find relevant information and download a copy of the registration form.
You are very welcome to come and meet us.
To find out when our next Informal Visit Days are please click the button below to book your appointment.

Welcome to the Snaresbrook Prep Parents’ Association (SPPA) page!
SPPA is the place to go if you feel like playing a more active part in the school and want to make life at school more fun for your child or children.
After an enforced break in fundraising activities due to the Covid related restrictions, the SPPA is now getting back up and running and we have a new committee for the current academic year.
Our constitution (which can be read at the bottom of this page) sets out our objectives which in summary are:

Funds raised are used to cover costs of events, to contribute towards the costs of some trips and also to fund other expenditure proposals that help us to meet our objectives (which are considered on a case by case basis).

Lower Foundation Stage

How can you get involved?
All parents, guardians and carers of pupils attending the school are automatically members of the SPPA and are invited to contribute ideas on how SPPA can help enhance school life.
We usually hold one official meeting per term with the participation of members of the Leadership Team. Dates are communicated in advance via class reps and by email from the school office. The meeting is typically at 8pm and all members are invited to attend and contribute.
Meetings are currently being held via Zoom.
You can get more involved in any event at any time throughout the year, regardless of which class or classes your child or children are in. We welcome volunteers to the committee including on an ad hoc basis for individual events.
We know that most parents have busy schedules so we believe a small contribution from lots of people is the easiest way to meet our objectives and enable us to run fun events for the children to take part in. You are welcome to be involved in as many events as you are willing and able to!
You can get in touch with us via your class rep, on the school forecourt or via email. : sppacommittee@outlook.com

Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Safeguarding within the Forest Group is the collective responsibility of all. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and young people in our care. Safeguarding is not just the role of one organisation or one person in an organisation, but the responsibility of us all, all of the time.
We maintain a proactive Safeguarding culture focused on earliest intervention. This is the most important work we do, and the work is never finished in Safeguarding and Child Protection. We exercise professional curiosity, and we pride ourselves on recognizing and knowing what to look out for in order to keep children safe. We want to encourage them to talk openly and enable them to feel confident that they will be listened to, and this is why we provide them with opportunities to discuss issues and report problems affecting their safety and wellbeing. We are alert to the signs of abuse and neglect and follow our procedures to ensure that all children and young people receive effective support, protection and guidance in order for them to feel safe.
Our priority is to create a safe, supportive and inclusive environment where children are safe and secure whilst ensuring they are known, liked and valued.
All members of the Forest Group community are considered Safeguarding Partners. This includes parents/carers and pupils. We all understand our collective responsibility in passing on Safeguarding information to keep ourselves and others safe.
In line with Keeping Children Safe in Education at Forest we maintain an attitude of “it could happen here”.
We follow robust safer recruitment practices in line with statutory guidance.
What do I do if I have a Safeguarding concern?
If you have a safeguarding concern about a child or young person that attends the school please contact the School Lead DSL, DDSL or the Forest Group DSL.
If you have a concern regarding an adult please contact the CEO/Warden of the Forest Group directly alternatively please contact the Head of Snaresbrook Prep.
During school hours – contact the School on 020 8989 2394 and ask to speak to one of the key safeguarding team.

We are approved for the purpose of inspection under Section 162A of the Education Act 2002, and report to the Department for Education on the extent to which schools meet statutory requirements. pageCache.pageTitle: Our School Grounds - Snaresbrook Prep School
pageCache.text:
The school occupies a substantial Victorian building in South Woodford, once a large private home which over time has been adapted to accommodate our classrooms and other facilities.
In a separate building to the rear of the main house is our school hall, used for daily assembly and to provide a full programme of physical education, music, drama, games and other extra-curricular activities. The hall is in use by children of all ages continually throughout the day.
Our Early Years Foundaton Stage department occupies a self-contained unit of two well-lit rooms with their own toilet facilities. A purpose built garden provides an outdoor space for play and practical activities for our youngest children and a play area which is laid with artificial grass is used by all the children during breaks and for outdoor actitvities.
For Years 3 – 6, we use Frenford Sports Club for sports & games lessons, Ashton Playing Fields for athletics and Caterham high school swimming pool for weekly swimming lessons.

The Early Years Foundation Stage at Snaresbrook Prep School is the period from age three to the end of the Upper Foundation Stage. It is a distinct stage and important both in its own right and in preparing children for later schooling. There are seven key areas of learning and development in the EYFS that must shape educational programmes in early years settings.
